title: Rape
bareActText: A man is said to commit “rape” if he— (a) penetrates his penis, to any extent, into the vagina, mouth, urethra or anus of a woman or makes her to do so with him or any other person; or (b) inserts, to any extent, any object or a part of the body, not being the penis, into the vagina, the urethra or anus of a woman or makes her to do so with him or any other person; or (c) manipulates any part of the body of a woman so as to cause penetration into the vagina, urethra, anus or any part of body of such woman or makes her to do so with him or any other person; or (d) applies his mouth to the vagina, anus, urethra of a woman or makes her to do so with him or any other person, under the circumstances falling under any of the following seven descriptions:— (i) against her will; (ii) without her consent; (iii) with her consent, when her consent has been obtained by putting her or any person in whom she is interested, in fear of death or of hurt; (iv) with her consent, when the man knows that he is not her husband and that her consent is given because she believes that he is another man to whom she is or believes herself to be lawfully married; (v) with her consent when, at the time of giving such consent, by reason of unsoundness of mind or intoxication or the administration by him personally or through another of any stupefying or unwholesome substance, she is unable to understand the nature and consequences of that to which she gives consent; (vi) with or without her consent, when she is under eighteen years of age; (vii) when she is unable to communicate consent. Explanation 1.—For the purposes of this section, “vagina” shall also include labia majora. Explanation 2.—Consent means an unequivocal voluntary agreement when the woman by words, gestures or any form of verbal or non-verbal communication, communicates willingness to participate in the specific sexual act: Provided that a woman who does not physically resist to the act of penetration shall not by the reason only of that fact, be regarded as consenting to the sexual activity. Exception 1.––A medical procedure or intervention shall not constitute rape. Exception 2.––Sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, the wife not being under eighteen years of age, is not rape.
plainMeaning: This section defines rape. A man commits rape if he does any of the four kinds of act listed in clauses (a) to (d) — penetration by the penis, insertion of an object or another body part, manipulation of the body to cause penetration, or application of the mouth — in any of seven circumstances: against her will; without her consent; with consent obtained by fear of death or hurt; with consent given because she believes he is her husband; with consent given when she cannot understand what she consents to because of unsoundness of mind, intoxication or a stupefying substance; when she is under eighteen, whether she consents or not; or when she cannot communicate consent. Consent must be an unequivocal, voluntary agreement communicated by words, gestures or other means, and the mere absence of physical resistance is not consent. A medical procedure is not rape, and sexual acts by a man with his own wife who is not under eighteen are not rape.
ingredients: The accused is a man; the victim is a woman
One of the acts in clauses (a) to (d) (penetrative or oral acts, to any extent)

Done in one of the seven circumstances: against her will; without consent; consent by fear; consent by impersonation of a husband; consent without understanding; she is under 18; she cannot communicate consent
Consent = unequivocal voluntary agreement; not resisting physically is not consent (Expl. 2)
Exception 1 — a medical procedure or intervention is not rape
Exception 2 — acts by a man with his own wife aged 18 or above are not rape
punishment: Not applicable — this section defines rape; punishment is set by ss.64-66, 70 and 71.

ipcReference.changeNote: Corresponds to s.375 IPC. The marital exception now protects only a wife under eighteen (the IPC text said fifteen); 'vagina includes labia majora' is Explanation 1.

illustrations: P gives Q a drink laced with a sedative, and while she is unable to understand what is happening he has intercourse with her. Her apparent agreement is not consent under clause (v); P commits rape.
R, aged 22, has intercourse with S, who is 17 and willing. Because S is under eighteen, clause (vi) applies and R commits rape even though S agreed.

title: Punishment for rape
bareActText: (1) Whoever, except in the cases provided for in sub-section (2), commits rape, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine. (2) Whoever,— (a) being a police officer, commits rape,— (i) within the limits of the police station to which such police officer is appointed; or (ii) in the premises of any station house; or (iii) on a woman in such police officer’s custody or in the custody of a police officer subordinate to such police officer; or (b) being a public servant, commits rape on a woman in such public servant’s custody or in the custody of a public servant subordinate to such public servant; or (c) being a member of the armed forces deployed in an area by the Central Government or a State Government commits rape in such area; or (d) being on the management or on the staff of a jail, remand home or other place of custody established by or under any law for the time being in force or of a women’s or children’s institution, commits rape on any inmate of such jail, remand home, place or institution; or (e) being on the management or on the staff of a hospital, commits rape on a woman in that hospital; or (f) being a relative, guardian or teacher of, or a person in a position of trust or authority towards the woman, commits rape on such woman; or (g) commits rape during communal or sectarian violence; or (h) commits rape on a woman knowing her to be pregnant; or (i) commits rape, on a woman incapable of giving consent; or (j) being in a position of control or dominance over a woman, commits rape on such woman; or (k) commits rape on a woman suffering from mental or physical disability; or (l) while committing rape causes grievous bodily harm or maims or disfigures or endangers the life of a woman; or (m) commits rape repeatedly on the same woman, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than ten years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, and shall also be liable to fine. Explanation.—For the purposes of this sub-section,— (a) “armed forces” means the naval, army and air forces and includes any member of the Armed Forces constituted under any law for the time being in force, including the paramilitary forces and any auxiliary forces that are under the control of the Central Government or the State Government; (b) “hospital” means the precincts of the hospital and includes the precincts of any institution for the reception and treatment of persons during convalescence or of persons requiring medical attention or rehabilitation; (c) “police officer” shall have the same meaning as assigned to the expression “police” under the Police Act, 1861; (d) “women’s or children’s institution” means an institution, whether called an orphanage or a home for neglected women or children or a widow’s home or an institution called by any other name, which is established and maintained for the reception and care of women or children.
plainMeaning: Sub-section (1) sets the basic punishment for rape: rigorous imprisonment of at least ten years, which may extend to life, plus fine. Sub-section (2) lists aggravated situations where the offender abuses a position or the victim is especially vulnerable — for example rape by a police officer within his station limits or on a woman in custody, by a public servant on a woman in his custody, by armed forces in an area of deployment, by jail or hospital staff, by a relative, guardian, teacher or person in trust or authority, during communal violence, on a pregnant woman, on a woman unable to consent or with a disability, rape causing grievous harm, or repeated rape. For these the minimum is still ten years, but the maximum is life imprisonment meaning the rest of the offender's natural life.
ingredients: s.64(1) — rape (as defined in s.63) not covered by s.64(2)

s.64(2) — rape in an aggravated situation: police officer, public servant, armed forces, jail/remand home/institution staff, hospital staff, relative/guardian/teacher/person in trust, communal violence, pregnant victim, victim incapable of consent, person in control or dominance, victim with disability, grievous harm, or repeated rape
The Explanation defines 'armed forces', 'hospital', 'police officer' and 'women's or children's institution'
punishment: (1) Rigorous imprisonment for not less than 10 years, which may extend to imprisonment for life, and fine. (2) Rigorous imprisonment for not less than 10 years, which may extend to imprisonment for life meaning the remainder of the person's natural life, and fine.

title: Punishment for rape in certain cases
bareActText: (1) Whoever, commits rape on a woman under sixteen years of age shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, and shall also be liable to fine: Provided that such fine shall be just and reasonable to meet the medical expenses and rehabilitation of the victim: Provided further that any fine imposed under this sub-section shall be paid to the victim. (2) Whoever, commits rape on a woman under twelve years of age shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, and with fine or with death: Provided that such fine shall be just and reasonable to meet the medical expenses and rehabilitation of the victim: Provided further that any fine imposed under this sub-section shall be paid to the victim.
plainMeaning: This section gives higher punishment when the victim is a young girl. Rape of a woman under sixteen carries rigorous imprisonment of at least twenty years, extending to life for the rest of natural life, plus fine. Rape of a woman under twelve carries the same minimum and maximum, or death. In both cases the fine must be just and reasonable to meet the victim's medical expenses and rehabilitation, and it is paid to the victim.
ingredients: Rape (as defined in s.63)
s.65(1) — the victim is under 16 years of age
s.65(2) — the victim is under 12 years of age
Fine must cover medical expenses and rehabilitation and is paid to the victim
punishment: (1) Under 16: rigorous imprisonment for not less than 20 years, extending to imprisonment for life (remainder of natural life), and fine. (2) Under 12: rigorous imprisonment for not less than 20 years, extending to imprisonment for life (remainder of natural life), and fine, or death.

title: Punishment for causing death or resulting in persistent vegetative state of victim
bareActText: Whoever, commits an offence punishable under sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) of section 64 and in the course of such commission inflicts an injury which causes the death of the woman or causes the woman to be in a persistent vegetative state, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, or with death.
plainMeaning: If, while committing rape punishable under s.64(1) or (2), the offender inflicts an injury that causes the woman's death or leaves her in a persistent vegetative state, the punishment rises to rigorous imprisonment of at least twenty years, extending to life for the rest of natural life, or death.
ingredients: Commission of an offence under s.64(1) or s.64(2)
In the course of it, infliction of an injury
The injury causes death, or a persistent vegetative state
punishment: Rigorous imprisonment for not less than 20 years, which may extend to imprisonment for life (remainder of natural life), or death.

title: Sexual intercourse by husband upon his wife during separation
bareActText: Whoever has sexual intercourse with his own wife, who is living separately, whether under a decree of separation or otherwise, without her consent, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than two years but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. Explanation.—In this section, “sexual intercourse” shall mean any of the acts mentioned in clauses (a) to (d) of section 63.
plainMeaning: A husband who has sexual intercourse (any act in clauses (a) to (d) of s.63) with his wife without her consent, while she is living separately — whether under a decree of separation or otherwise — is punished with two to seven years' imprisonment and fine. It is cognizable only on the complaint of the victim.
ingredients: The accused is the husband
The wife is living separately (under a decree or otherwise)
Sexual intercourse (any act in s.63(a)-(d)) with her
Without her consent
punishment: Imprisonment of either description for not less than 2 years, which may extend to 7 years, and fine.

title: Sexual intercourse by a person in authority
bareActText: Whoever, being— (a) in a position of authority or in a fiduciary relationship; or (b) a public servant; or (c) superintendent or manager of a jail, remand home or other place of custody established by or under any law for the time being in force, or a women’s or children’s institution; or (d) on the management of a hospital or being on the staff of a hospital, abuses such position or fiduciary relationship to induce or seduce any woman either in his custody or under his charge or present in the premises to have sexual intercourse with him, such sexual intercourse not amounting to the offence of rape, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than five years, but which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. Explanation 1.—In this section, “sexual intercourse” shall mean any of the acts mentioned in clauses (a) to (d) of section 63. Explanation 2.—For the purposes of this section, Explanation 1 to section 63 shall also be applicable. Explanation 3.—“Superintendent”, in relation to a jail, remand home or other place of custody or a women’s or children’s institution, includes a person holding any other office in such jail, remand home, place or institution by virtue of which such person can exercise any authority or control over its inmates. Explanation 4.—The expressions “hospital” and “women’s or children’s institution” shall respectively have the same meanings as in clauses (b) and (d) of the Explanation to sub-section (2) of section 64.
plainMeaning: This section punishes a person who abuses a position of authority or trust to induce or seduce a woman in his custody, under his charge or present in the premises into sexual intercourse that does not amount to rape. It covers a person in authority or a fiduciary relationship, a public servant, the superintendent or manager of a jail, remand home, place of custody or women's or children's institution, and hospital management or staff. The punishment is rigorous imprisonment of five to ten years and fine.

He abuses that position or relationship
To induce or seduce a woman in his custody, under his charge, or present in the premises
Sexual intercourse follows, not amounting to rape
punishment: Rigorous imprisonment for not less than 5 years, which may extend to 10 years, and fine.

title: Sexual intercourse by employing deceitful means, etc.
bareActText: Whoever, by deceitful means or by making promise to marry to a woman without any intention of fulfilling the same, has sexual intercourse with her, such sexual intercourse not amounting to the offence of rape, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years and shall also be liable to fine. Explanation.—“deceitful means” shall include inducement for, or false promise of employment or promotion, or marrying by suppressing identity.
plainMeaning: New in the BNS. A person who has sexual intercourse with a woman by deceitful means, or by promising to marry her with no intention of keeping the promise, commits an offence where the act does not amount to rape. 'Deceitful means' include inducing her with, or falsely promising, a job or a promotion, and marrying her while hiding one's identity. The punishment is up to ten years and fine.
ingredients: Sexual intercourse with a woman
Obtained by deceitful means, or by a promise to marry made with no intention of fulfilling it
Deceitful means include inducement or false promise of employment or promotion, and marrying by suppressing identity
The act does not amount to rape
punishment: Imprisonment of either description which may extend to 10 years, and fine.

title: Gang rape
bareActText: (1) Where a woman is raped by one or more persons constituting a group or acting in furtherance of a common intention, each of those persons shall be deemed to have committed the offence of rape and shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, and with fine: Provided that such fine shall be just and reasonable to meet the medical expenses and rehabilitation of the victim: Provided further that any fine imposed under this sub-section shall be paid to the victim. (2) Where a woman under eighteen years of age is raped by one or more persons constituting a group or acting in furtherance of a common intention, each of those persons shall be deemed to have committed the offence of rape and shall be punished with imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, and with fine, or with death: Provided that such fine shall be just and reasonable to meet the medical expenses and rehabilitation of the victim: Provided further that any fine imposed under this sub-section shall be paid to the victim.
plainMeaning: Where a woman is raped by one or more persons forming a group or acting in furtherance of a common intention, each of them is treated as having committed rape. Sub-section (1) prescribes rigorous imprisonment of at least twenty years, extending to life for the rest of natural life, and fine. Sub-section (2), where the woman is under eighteen, prescribes life imprisonment for the rest of natural life and fine, or death. In both cases the fine must cover medical expenses and rehabilitation and is paid to the victim.
ingredients: Rape of a woman by one or more persons
Constituting a group or acting in furtherance of a common intention
Each person is deemed to have committed rape
s.70(2) — the woman is under 18 years of age
punishment: (1) Rigorous imprisonment for not less than 20 years, extending to imprisonment for life (remainder of natural life), and fine. (2) Under 18: imprisonment for life (remainder of natural life) and fine, or death.

title: Punishment for repeat offenders
bareActText: Whoever has been previously convicted of an offence punishable under section 64 or section 65 or section 66 or section 70 and is subsequently convicted of an offence punishable under any of the said sections shall be punished with imprisonment for life which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person’s natural life, or with death.
plainMeaning: A person who, after being convicted of an offence under s.64, 65, 66 or 70, is again convicted of an offence under any of those sections must be punished with life imprisonment for the rest of natural life, or death.

A subsequent conviction under any of those sections

title: Disclosure of identity of victim of certain offences, etc.
bareActText: (1) Whoever prints or publishes the name or any matter which may make known the identity of any person against whom an offence under section 64 or section 65 or section 66 or section 67 or section 68 or section 69 or section 70 or section 71 is alleged or found to have been committed (hereafter in this section referred to as the victim) shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years and shall also be liable to fine. (2) Nothing in sub-section (1) extends to any printing or publication of the name or any matter which may make known the identity of the victim if such printing or publication is— (a) by or under the order in writing of the officer-in-charge of the police station or the police officer making the investigation into such offence acting in good faith for the purposes of such investigation; or (b) by, or with the authorisation in writing of, the victim; or (c) where the victim is dead or a child or of unsound mind, by, or with the authorisation in writing of, the next of kin of the victim: Provided that no such authorisation shall be given by the next of kin to anybody other than the chairman or the secretary, by whatever name called, of any recognised welfare institution or organisation. Explanation.—For the purposes of this sub-section, “recognised welfare institution or organisation” means a social welfare institution or organisation recognised in this behalf by the Central Government or the State Government.
plainMeaning: Printing or publishing a victim's name, or anything that may reveal her identity, in cases under ss.64 to 71 is punishable with up to two years and fine. Disclosure is allowed only when made by or under a written order of the police officer investigating in good faith, by or with the written authorisation of the victim, or — where the victim is dead, a child or of unsound mind — with the written authorisation of her next of kin, who may give it only to the chairman or secretary of a recognised welfare institution or organisation.

The victim is a person against whom an offence under ss.64-71 is alleged or found
Not covered by an exception in s.72(2): police investigation in good faith; victim's written authorisation; next of kin's written authorisation to a recognised welfare body
punishment: Imprisonment of either description which may extend to 2 years, and fine.

title: Printing or publishing any matter relating to Court proceedings without permission
bareActText: Whoever prints or publishes any matter in relation to any proceeding before a Court with respect to an offence referred to in section 72 without the previous permission of such Court shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years and shall also be liable to fine. Explanation.—The printing or publication of the judgment of any High Court or the Supreme Court does not amount to an offence within the meaning of this section.
plainMeaning: Printing or publishing anything about court proceedings relating to an offence referred to in s.72 without the previous permission of that court is punishable with up to two years and fine. Publishing a judgment of a High Court or the Supreme Court is not an offence.

The proceeding concerns an offence referred to in s.72
Without the previous permission of that court
Publication of High Court or Supreme Court judgments is excluded

title: Assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty
bareActText: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.
plainMeaning: Assaulting or using criminal force on a woman, intending to outrage her modesty or knowing that it is likely to do so, is punishable with one to five years and fine.

On a woman
With intent to outrage her modesty, or knowing it is likely to outrage it

title: Sexual harassment
bareActText: (1) A man committing any of the following acts:— (i) physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures; or (ii) a demand or request for sexual favours; or (iii) showing pornography against the will of a woman; or (iv) making sexually coloured remarks, shall be guilty of the offence of sexual harassment. (2) Any man who commits the offence specified in clause (i) or clause (ii) or clause (iii) of sub-section (1) shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. (3) Any man who commits the offence specified in clause (iv) of sub-section (1) shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
plainMeaning: A man commits sexual harassment if he makes unwelcome physical contact and explicit sexual advances, demands or requests sexual favours, shows pornography to a woman against her will, or makes sexually coloured remarks. The first three are punishable with rigorous imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both; sexually coloured remarks with imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both.

(i) Unwelcome physical contact and explicit sexual overtures; or (ii) demand or request for sexual favours; or (iii) showing pornography against her will; or (iv) sexually coloured remarks

title: Assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to disrobe
bareActText: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman or abets such act with the intention of disrobing or compelling her to be naked, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
plainMeaning: Assaulting or using criminal force on a woman, or abetting it, with the intention of disrobing her or forcing her to be naked, is punishable with three to seven years and fine.
ingredients: Assault or use of criminal force on a woman, or abetment of it
With the intention of disrobing her or compelling her to be naked
punishment: Imprisonment of either description for not less than 3 years, which may extend to 7 years, and fine.

title: Voyeurism
bareActText: Whoever watches, or captures the image of a woman engaging in a private act in circumstances where she would usually have the expectation of not being observed either by the perpetrator or by any other person at the behest of the perpetrator or disseminates such image shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year, but which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine, and be punished on a second or subsequent conviction, with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than three years, but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. Explanation 1.—For the purposes of this section, “private act” includes an act of watching carried out in a place which, in the circumstances, would reasonably be expected to provide privacy and where the victim’s genitals, posterior or breasts are exposed or covered only in underwear; or the victim is using a lavatory; or the victim is doing a sexual act that is not of a kind ordinarily done in public. Explanation 2.—Where the victim consents to the capture of the images or any act, but not to their dissemination to third persons and where such image or act is disseminated, such dissemination shall be considered an offence under this section.
plainMeaning: A person who watches or captures the image of a woman engaged in a private act, where she would expect not to be observed, or who spreads such an image, commits voyeurism. A 'private act' includes situations where her intimate parts are exposed or covered only by underwear, where she is using a lavatory, or where she is doing a sexual act not ordinarily done in public. Even if she consented to the picture being taken, spreading it to others without her consent is an offence. The first conviction carries one to three years and fine; a second or later conviction three to seven years and fine.
ingredients: Watching, or capturing an image of, a woman engaging in a private act
In circumstances where she would expect not to be observed (by the offender or anyone at his behest)
Or disseminating such an image
Consent to capture is not consent to dissemination (Expl. 2)
punishment: First conviction: imprisonment of either description for not less than 1 year, which may extend to 3 years, and fine. Second or subsequent conviction: not less than 3 years, which may extend to 7 years, and fine.

title: Stalking
bareActText: (1) Any man who— (i) follows a woman and contacts, or attempts to contact such woman to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by such woman; or (ii) monitors the use by a woman of the internet, e-mail or any other form of electronic communication, commits the offence of stalking: Provided that such conduct shall not amount to stalking if the man who pursued it proves that— (i) it was pursued for the purpose of preventing or detecting crime and the man accused of stalking had been entrusted with the responsibility of prevention and detection of crime by the State; or (ii) it was pursued under any law or to comply with any condition or requirement imposed by any person under any law; or (iii) in the particular circumstances such conduct was reasonable and justified. (2) Whoever commits the offence of stalking shall be punished on first conviction with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine; and be punished on a second or subsequent conviction, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.
plainMeaning: A man stalks a woman if he follows her and contacts, or tries to contact, her repeatedly to build personal interaction despite her clear lack of interest, or if he monitors her use of the internet, e-mail or other electronic communication. It is not stalking if he proves the conduct was for preventing or detecting crime under State authority, was done under a law, or was reasonable and justified in the circumstances. The first conviction carries up to three years and fine; a second or later conviction up to five years and fine.
ingredients: The accused is a man; the victim is a woman
(i) Following and contacting or attempting to contact her repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest; or (ii) monitoring her internet, e-mail or electronic communication
Defences (burden on the accused): crime prevention/detection under State authority; done under any law; reasonable and justified
punishment: First conviction: imprisonment of either description up to 3 years, and fine. Second or subsequent conviction: up to 5 years, and fine.

title: Word, gesture or act intended to insult modesty of a woman
bareActText: Whoever, intending to insult the modesty of any woman, utters any words, makes any sound or gesture, or exhibits any object in any form, intending that such word or sound shall be heard, or that such gesture or object shall be seen, by such woman, or intrudes upon the privacy of such woman, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and also with fine.
plainMeaning: Uttering words, making sounds or gestures, or showing any object, intending that a woman hear or see it and intending to insult her modesty, or intruding on her privacy, is punishable with simple imprisonment up to three years and fine. The woman may compound it with the court's permission.
ingredients: Intention to insult the modesty of a woman
Uttering words, making a sound or gesture, or exhibiting an object, intending her to hear or see it; or intruding upon her privacy
punishment: Simple imprisonment which may extend to 3 years, and fine.

title: Dowry death
bareActText: (1) Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called “dowry death”, and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death. Explanation.—For the purposes of this sub-section, “dowry” shall have the same meaning as in section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961. (2) Whoever commits dowry death shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life.
plainMeaning: A 'dowry death' occurs where a woman dies by burns or bodily injury, or otherwise than under normal circumstances, within seven years of her marriage, and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or his relative for, or in connection with, a demand for dowry. The husband or relative is then deemed to have caused her death. 'Dowry' has the meaning in s.2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961. The punishment is at least seven years, extending to life.
ingredients: Death of a woman by burns, bodily injury, or otherwise than under normal circumstances
Within 7 years of her marriage
Soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment
By her husband or a relative of her husband
For, or in connection with, a demand for dowry
Effect: the husband or relative is deemed to have caused her death
punishment: Imprisonment for not less than 7 years, which may extend to imprisonment for life.

classification.compoundable: Not compoundable (not listed in BNSS s.359)

title: Cohabitation caused by man deceitfully inducing belief of lawful marriage
bareActText: Every man who by deceit causes any woman who is not lawfully married to him to believe that she is lawfully married to him and to cohabit or have sexual intercourse with him in that belief, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
plainMeaning: A man who by deceit makes a woman believe that she is lawfully married to him, when she is not, and causes her to live with him or have sexual intercourse with him in that belief, is punishable with up to ten years and fine.
ingredients: The accused is a man
By deceit, he causes a woman not lawfully married to him to believe that she is
She cohabits or has sexual intercourse with him in that belief
punishment: Imprisonment of either description which may extend to 10 years, and fine.

title: Marrying again during lifetime of husband or wife
bareActText: (1) Whoever, having a husband or wife living, marries in any case in which such marriage is void by reason of its taking place during the life of such husband or wife, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. Exception.—This sub-section does not extend to any person whose marriage with such husband or wife has been declared void by a Court of competent jurisdiction, nor to any person who contracts a marriage during the life of a former husband or wife, if such husband or wife, at the time of the subsequent marriage, shall have been continually absent from such person for the space of seven years, and shall not have been heard of by such person as being alive within that time provided the person contracting such subsequent marriage shall, before such marriage takes place, inform the person with whom such marriage is contracted of the real state of facts so far as the same are within his or her knowledge. (2) Whoever commits the offence under sub-section (1) having concealed from the person with whom the subsequent marriage is contracted, the fact of the former marriage, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
plainMeaning: Sub-section (1) punishes a person who, having a living husband or wife, marries again where that marriage is void because the first spouse is alive (bigamy): up to seven years and fine. The Exception excludes a person whose earlier marriage was declared void by a competent court, and a person whose spouse has been continually absent and not heard of as alive for seven years, provided the new partner is told the real facts before the marriage. Sub-section (2) raises the punishment to ten years and fine where the earlier marriage is concealed from the new partner.
ingredients: A husband or wife is living
The accused marries again
The second marriage is void because it takes place during the life of the spouse
Exception: first marriage declared void by a court, or spouse absent and unheard of for 7 years and the facts disclosed to the new partner
s.82(2) — the former marriage is concealed from the new partner
punishment: (1) Imprisonment of either description up to 7 years, and fine. (2) With concealment of the former marriage: up to 10 years, and fine.

title: Marriage ceremony fraudulently gone through without lawful marriage
bareActText: Whoever, dishonestly or with a fraudulent intention, goes through the ceremony of being married, knowing that he is not thereby lawfully married, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
plainMeaning: A person who, dishonestly or with fraudulent intention, goes through a marriage ceremony knowing that it does not create a lawful marriage is punishable with up to seven years and fine.
ingredients: Going through a ceremony of being married
Knowing that he is not thereby lawfully married
Dishonestly or with a fraudulent intention
punishment: Imprisonment of either description which may extend to 7 years, and fine.

title: Enticing or taking away or detaining with criminal intent a married woman
bareActText: Whoever takes or entices away any woman who is and whom he knows or has reason to believe to be the wife of any other man, with intent that she may have illicit intercourse with any person, or conceals or detains with that intent any such woman, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
plainMeaning: Taking or enticing away a woman whom the accused knows, or has reason to believe, is another man's wife, with intent that she may have illicit intercourse with any person, or concealing or detaining her with that intent, is punishable with up to two years, or fine, or both. The husband and the woman may compound it; under BNSS s.219(2) only the husband is treated as aggrieved for filing a complaint.
ingredients: Taking or enticing away, or concealing or detaining, a woman
She is the wife of another man, and the accused knows or has reason to believe so
With intent that she may have illicit intercourse with any person
punishment: Imprisonment of either description up to 2 years, or fine, or both.

title: Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty
bareActText: Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
plainMeaning: A husband, or a relative of the husband, who subjects a woman to cruelty (as defined in s.86) is punishable with up to three years and fine. It is cognizable when information is given to the police by the aggrieved woman, a relative of hers by blood, marriage or adoption, or, if there is none, a notified public servant.
ingredients: The accused is the husband or a relative of the husband
He or she subjects the woman to cruelty as defined in s.86
punishment: Imprisonment which may extend to 3 years, and fine.

title: Cruelty defined
bareActText: For the purposes of section 85, “cruelty” means— (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.
plainMeaning: For s.85, 'cruelty' means (a) any wilful conduct likely to drive the woman to suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to her life, limb or physical or mental health, or (b) harassing her to force her or her relatives to meet an unlawful demand for property or valuable security, or because they failed to meet such a demand.
ingredients: (a) Wilful conduct likely to drive her to suicide, or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (mental or physical); or
(b) Harassment to coerce her or her relatives to meet an unlawful demand for property or valuable security, or because of failure to meet it
punishment: Not applicable — this section defines cruelty for s.85.

title: Kidnapping, abducting or inducing woman to compel her marriage, etc.
bareActText: Whoever kidnaps or abducts any woman with intent that she may be compelled, or knowing it to be likely that she will be compelled, to marry any person against her will, or in order that she may be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse, or knowing it to be likely that she will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and whoever, by means of criminal intimidation as defined in this Sanhita or of abuse of authority or any other method of compulsion, induces any woman to go from any place with intent that she may be, or knowing that it is likely that she will be, forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person shall also be punishable as aforesaid.
plainMeaning: Kidnapping or abducting a woman intending, or knowing it likely, that she will be forced to marry against her will or forced or seduced into illicit intercourse is punishable with up to ten years and fine. The same punishment applies to inducing a woman, by criminal intimidation, abuse of authority or other compulsion, to go from any place with that intent or knowledge.
ingredients: Kidnapping or abducting a woman; or inducing her to go from any place by criminal intimidation, abuse of authority or other compulsion
Intending, or knowing it likely, that she will be compelled to marry against her will, or forced or seduced to illicit intercourse
punishment: Imprisonment of either description which may extend to 10 years, and fine.

title: Causing miscarriage
bareActText: Whoever voluntarily causes a woman with child to miscarry, shall, if such miscarriage be not caused in good faith for the purpose of saving the life of the woman, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both; and, if the woman be quick with child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. Explanation.—A woman who causes herself to miscarry, is within the meaning of this section.
plainMeaning: Voluntarily causing a pregnant woman to miscarry, unless done in good faith to save her life, is punishable with up to three years, or fine, or both; if she is 'quick with child' (the baby's movement can be felt), up to seven years and fine. A woman who causes her own miscarriage is also covered. The woman may compound it with the court's permission.
ingredients: Voluntarily causing a woman with child to miscarry
Not in good faith to save the woman's life
Higher punishment if the woman is quick with child
A woman who causes herself to miscarry is covered (Explanation)
punishment: Imprisonment of either description up to 3 years, or fine, or both; if the woman is quick with child, up to 7 years and fine.

title: Causing miscarriage without woman's consent
bareActText: Whoever commits the offence under section 88 without the consent of the woman, whether the woman is quick with child or not, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
plainMeaning: Causing a miscarriage under s.88 without the woman's consent, whether or not she is quick with child, is punishable with life imprisonment, or up to ten years and fine.
ingredients: The offence under s.88
Without the consent of the woman
Whether or not she is quick with child
punishment: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, and fine.

title: Death caused by act done with intent to cause miscarriage
bareActText: (1) Whoever, with intent to cause the miscarriage of a woman with child, does any act which causes the death of such woman, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. (2) Where the act referred to in sub-section (1) is done without the consent of the woman, shall be punishable either with imprisonment for life, or with the punishment specified in said sub-section. Explanation.—It is not essential to this offence that the offender should know that the act is likely to cause death.
plainMeaning: If an act done with intent to cause a pregnant woman's miscarriage causes her death, the offender is punishable with up to ten years and fine; if the act was done without her consent, with life imprisonment or that punishment. The offender need not know that the act was likely to cause death.
ingredients: An act done with intent to cause miscarriage of a woman with child
The act causes her death
s.90(2) — done without her consent
Knowledge that the act is likely to cause death is not required
punishment: (1) Imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, and fine. (2) Without consent: imprisonment for life, or as in (1).

title: Act done with intent to prevent child being born alive or to cause to die after birth
bareActText: Whoever before the birth of any child does any act with the intention of thereby preventing that child from being born alive or causing it to die after its birth, and does by such act prevent that child from being born alive, or causes it to die after its birth, shall, if such act be not caused in good faith for the purpose of saving the life of the mother, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, or with fine, or with both.
plainMeaning: Doing an act before a child's birth intending to prevent it from being born alive, or to cause it to die after birth, and thereby causing that result, is punishable with up to ten years, or fine, or both, unless done in good faith to save the mother's life.
ingredients: An act before the birth of a child
Intending to prevent it from being born alive, or to cause it to die after birth
The act does prevent live birth or cause death after birth
Not in good faith to save the mother's life
punishment: Imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, or fine, or both.

title: Causing death of quick unborn child by act amounting to culpable homicide
bareActText: Whoever does any act under such circumstances, that if he thereby caused death he would be guilty of culpable homicide, and does by such act cause the death of a quick unborn child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. Illustration. A, knowing that he is likely to cause the death of a pregnant woman, does an act which, if it caused the death of the woman, would amount to culpable homicide. The woman is injured, but does not die; but the death of an unborn quick child with which she is pregnant is thereby caused. A is guilty of the offence defined in this section.
plainMeaning: Doing an act in circumstances in which causing death would be culpable homicide, and thereby causing the death of a quick unborn child, is punishable with up to ten years and fine.
ingredients: An act done in circumstances that would make it culpable homicide if it caused death
The act causes the death of a quick unborn child
punishment: Imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, and fine.

title: Exposure and abandonment of child under twelve years of age, by parent or person having care of it
bareActText: Whoever being the father or mother of a child under the age of twelve years, or having the care of such child, shall expose or leave such child in any place with the intention of wholly abandoning such child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both. Explanation.—This section is not intended to prevent the trial of the offender for murder or culpable homicide, as the case may be, if the child die in consequence of the exposure.
plainMeaning: A father, mother or other person caring for a child under twelve who exposes or leaves the child anywhere intending to abandon it completely is punishable with up to seven years, or fine, or both. If the child dies as a result, the offender may also be tried for murder or culpable homicide.
ingredients: The accused is the father or mother, or has care of the child
The child is under 12 years of age
Exposing or leaving the child in any place
With the intention of wholly abandoning the child
punishment: Imprisonment of either description up to 7 years, or fine, or both.

illustrations: K leaves her four-year-old son at a railway station and boards a train, intending never to return. K is guilty under s.93.

title: Concealment of birth by secret disposal of dead body
bareActText: Whoever, by secretly burying or otherwise disposing of the dead body of a child whether such child die before or after or during its birth, intentionally conceals or endeavours to conceal the birth of such child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
plainMeaning: Secretly burying or otherwise disposing of a child's dead body, whether the child died before, during or after birth, to intentionally conceal or try to conceal the birth, is punishable with up to two years, or fine, or both.
ingredients: Secret burial or other disposal of the dead body of a child
The child died before, during or after birth
Intention to conceal, or an attempt to conceal, the birth
punishment: Imprisonment of either description up to 2 years, or fine, or both.

title: Hiring, employing or engaging a child to commit an offence
bareActText: Whoever hires, employs or engages any child to commit an offence shall be punished with imprisonment of either description which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to ten years, and with fine; and if the offence be committed shall also be punished with the punishment provided for that offence as if the offence has been committed by such person himself. Explanation.—Hiring, employing, engaging or using a child for sexual exploitation or pornography is covered within the meaning of this section.
plainMeaning: New in the BNS. Hiring, employing or engaging a child to commit an offence is punishable with three to ten years and fine. If the offence is committed, the person is also punished as if he had committed it himself. Using a child for sexual exploitation or pornography is covered.
ingredients: Hiring, employing or engaging (or using) a child
To commit an offence
If the offence is committed, additional liability as the principal offender
Includes using a child for sexual exploitation or pornography
punishment: Imprisonment of either description for not less than 3 years, which may extend to 10 years, and fine; and if the offence is committed, also the punishment for that offence.

title: Procuration of child
bareActText: Whoever, by any means whatsoever, induces any child to go from any place or to do any act with intent that such child may be, or knowing that it is likely that such child will be, forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
plainMeaning: Inducing a child, by any means, to go from any place or do any act, intending or knowing it likely that the child will be forced or seduced into illicit intercourse with another person, is punishable with up to ten years and fine.
ingredients: Inducing a child, by any means, to go from any place or to do any act
Intending, or knowing it likely, that the child will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person
punishment: Imprisonment which may extend to 10 years, and fine.

title: Kidnapping or abducting child under ten years of age with intent to steal from its person
bareActText: Whoever kidnaps or abducts any child under the age of ten years with the intention of taking dishonestly any movable property from the person of such child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
plainMeaning: Kidnapping or abducting a child under ten intending to dishonestly take movable property from the child's person is punishable with up to seven years and fine.
ingredients: Kidnapping or abducting a child
The child is under 10 years of age
With intent to take dishonestly movable property from the child's person
punishment: Imprisonment of either description up to 7 years, and fine.

title: Selling child for purposes of prostitution, etc.
bareActText: Whoever sells, lets to hire, or otherwise disposes of any child with intent that such child shall at any age be employed or used for the purpose of prostitution or illicit intercourse with any person or for any unlawful and immoral purpose, or knowing it to be likely that such child will at any age be employed or used for any such purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. Explanation 1.—When a female under the age of eighteen years is sold, let for hire, or otherwise disposed of to a prostitute or to any person who keeps or manages a brothel, the person so disposing of such female shall, until the contrary is proved, be presumed to have disposed of her with the intent that she shall be used for the purpose of prostitution. Explanation 2.—For the purposes of this section “illicit intercourse” means sexual intercourse between persons not united by marriage or by any union or tie which, though not amounting to a marriage, is recognised by the personal law or custom of the community to which they belong or, where they belong to different communities, of both such communities, as constituting between them a quasi-marital relation.
plainMeaning: Selling, letting for hire or otherwise disposing of a child, intending or knowing it likely that the child will at any age be used for prostitution, illicit intercourse or any unlawful and immoral purpose, is punishable with up to ten years and fine. Where a girl under eighteen is disposed of to a prostitute or brothel-keeper, the intent is presumed until the contrary is proved.
ingredients: Selling, letting to hire or otherwise disposing of a child
Intending, or knowing it likely, that the child will at any age be used for prostitution, illicit intercourse or an unlawful and immoral purpose
Presumption of intent where a girl under 18 is disposed of to a prostitute or brothel-keeper (Expl. 1)
'Illicit intercourse' defined (Expl. 2)
punishment: Imprisonment of either description up to 10 years, and fine.

classification.compoundable: Not compoundable (not listed in BNSS s.359)

ipcReference.changeNote: Corresponds to s.372 IPC; applies to any 'child' rather than a 'person under the age of eighteen years'.

illustrations: P sells his niece to a brothel-keeper. Under Explanation 1 he is presumed to have intended her to be used for prostitution, and is liable under s.98.

title: Buying child for purposes of prostitution, etc.
bareActText: Whoever buys, hires or otherwise obtains possession of any child with intent that such child shall at any age be employed or used for the purpose of prostitution or illicit intercourse with any person or for any unlawful and immoral purpose, or knowing it to be likely that such child will at any age be employed or used for any such purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to fourteen years, and shall also be liable to fine. Explanation 1.—Any prostitute or any person keeping or managing a brothel, who buys, hires or otherwise obtains possession of a female under the age of eighteen years shall, until the contrary is proved, be presumed to have obtained possession of such female with the intent that she shall be used for the purpose of prostitution. Explanation 2.—“Illicit intercourse” has the same meaning as in section 98.
plainMeaning: Buying, hiring or otherwise obtaining possession of a child, intending or knowing it likely that the child will at any age be used for prostitution, illicit intercourse or any unlawful and immoral purpose, is punishable with seven to fourteen years and fine. A prostitute or brothel-keeper who obtains a girl under eighteen is presumed to have that intent until the contrary is proved.
ingredients: Buying, hiring or otherwise obtaining possession of a child
Intending, or knowing it likely, that the child will at any age be used for prostitution, illicit intercourse or an unlawful and immoral purpose
Presumption against a prostitute or brothel-keeper obtaining a girl under 18 (Expl. 1)
punishment: Imprisonment of either description for not less than 7 years, which may extend to 14 years, and fine.

classification.compoundable: Not compoundable (not listed in BNSS s.359)
